title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཏེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 178)
shelf_note: Derge woodblock folio (margin 'ཏེ', Pramana section) from a commentary refuting materialism with the lamp/light analogy (support and supported, mind-body, rebirth): squarely Pramana Tengyur.

ocr_errors.image: possibly 'སྒྲོན་མ་ལས་དེ་མ་ཡིན་པ' (the glyph after མ looks like ལས at this resolution)
ocr_errors.problem: if the print has ལས, the sense is 'light does not move FROM the lamp to something else', and both translations stumble on 'or'

ocr_errors.image: འདུག་པ་ཡང་ / དེ་འགྱུར་ན (as far as can be read)
ocr_errors.problem: small orthographic normalisations that do not change the meaning

tr_errors_A.english: even though they do not share the same foundation or location
tr_errors_A.problem: the 'base and what abides in it' (container/contained) sense of support is turned into 'sharing a foundation or location'

tr_errors_A.english: rather, it is the intellect itself, such as wisdom and so on, that changes
tr_errors_A.problem: the claim 'wisdom and the rest are the mind itself' is recast: wisdom becomes an example of intellect, and 'that changes' is added

tr_errors_A.english: does not transfer elsewhere, whether to another lamp or anything else
tr_errors_A.problem: adds 'another' lamp; the source is about light not moving from or apart from the lamp
verse form lost (T16), and the conditional 'if everything with a support ... then' is given as flat assertions

tr_errors_B.english: consciousness supported by the body, even if directed toward another object, will also be destroyed
tr_errors_B.problem: ཡུལ་གཞན་ལ་གནས་པ here parallels the lamp-light 'located in another place'; 'directed toward another object' loses the spatial analogy

tr_errors_B.english: that light does not migrate to the lamp or to anything else
tr_errors_B.problem: 'migrate to the lamp' makes little sense; the point is that light does not move off from the lamp to something else
attributes the page to Dharmakirti, although the page is a commentary that cites verses and the book metadata names no author

pages.prefer_reason: Neither has a serious error, but B gets the container/contained relation and the 'wisdom etc. are the mind itself' clause right, and it keeps the summary verses as verse; its own slips are smaller.

book_verdict: A clean Derge Pramana folio with a good transcription. Both English versions are faithful in outline. Each has a moderate slip in the lamp/light argument, and B is the better reading.
